title: Email: Fw: STEVE'S SWAN SONG WEEK

Anthony Fenech
Tigers beat writer
Detroit Free Press
(734) 752-9667
Twitter: @anthonyfenech
From: Bull, Kevin <kbull@freepress.com>
Sent: Sunday, December 13, 2015 9:20 AM
To: Birkett, David <dbirkett@freepress.com>; Brudenell, Mike <mbrudenell@freepress.com>; Collison, Bill <bcollison@freepress.com>; Cotsonika, Nicholas <ncotsonika@freepress.com>; Crawford, Kirkland <kcrawford@freepress.com>; Darby, David <dfdarby@freepress.com>; Ellis, Vince <vellis@freepress.com>; Farrell, Perry <pafarrell@freepress.com>; Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>; Ford, Ryan <rford@freepress.com>; Jahnke, James <jjahnke@freepress.com>; Manzullo, Brian <bmanzullo@freepress.com>; Marcinkoski, Tim <tmarcinkoski@freepress.com>; McCabe, Mick <mmccabe@freepress.com>; Monarrez, Carlos <cmonarrez@freepress.com>; Rexrode, Joe <jrexrode@freepress.com>; St. James, Helene <hstjames@freepress.com>; Schrader, Steve <sschrader@freepress.com>; Sharp, Drew <dsharp@freepress.com>; Seidel, Jeff <jseidel@freepress.com>; Sipple, George <gsipple@freepress.com>; Snider, Lee <lsnider@freepress.com>; Snyder, Mark <msnyder@freepress.com>; Tarsha, Jeff <jtarsha@freepress.com>; Windsor, Shawn <swindsor@freepress.com>; Robles Hernandez, Dora <drobles@freepress.com>; Alter, Marlowe <malter@freepress.com>; familyonlypls@gmail.com <familyonlypls@gmail.com>
Cc: Bull, Kevin <kbull@freepress.com>
Subject: STEVE'S SWAN SONG WEEK 
 
All:

You probably heard from the staff announcement by Robert Huschka a few weeks ago in the office, but if not, I want everyone to know this will be Steve Schrader’s last week. He’s accepting an early retirement/separation offer after 30 fabulous years at the Free Press. His last day will be Friday.

There will be a sendoff around 4 p.m. at the hub for Steve and the other dozen or so early retirees. There’s also a party set for Tuesday to celebrate the early retirees, though Steve says he likely will not attend since he’s gonna have a busy week. The party will be at 6:30 at Firebird Tavern on Monroe downtown if interested.

From first-rate editor to staff humorist to agenda-setter to book editor to word doctor, Steve has supplied enormous amounts of leadership, creativity, energy and elbow grease over the years. Steve always has improved every piece of copy he touches — and tops it with a snappy headline. And who else could provide breaking coverage of locals in Dancing With The Stars and dozens of other reality TV shows? But his legacy at the Free Press always will be how he provides one of the few places in a newspaper (on now online) where readers can find actual humor. That’s why Gene always referred to Steve as “The Ol’ Humorist.” Over the years, he has been the czar of Super Sunday, Extra Points, The Ticker, The Puck, Second Season, Morning Line and so on, but whatever we call it, he delivers the news and views you can use — and the smile we all crave.
Here is a sampling of what people have said about Steve over the years:
If you’re looking to snap out of your Wings funk, take a look at today’s Octopus Garden. Steve Schrader’s package will bring a smile to your face.
-- Julie Topping, April 18, 2003

How did we engage and surprise readers today? In Morning Line, Steve Schrader had my favorite line of the day, in an item about how 25,000 fans at an upcoming Tigers game will get to take part in a mass magic trick. Here’s an excerpt: Tigers president Dave Dombrowski said: “You will have to see it to believe it.” You got that right – 25,000 people at Comerica Park?
-- Julie Topping, June 5, 2003

And Steve Schrader, once again, gets the line of the day, while also managing to work the Ford angle into Sports, with this Two Cents Worth on 2C: Ford chairman/CEO William Clay Ford Jr. notes in Newsweek that it’s tough for him to go out in public because “everybody’s a car expert and everybody’s a football expert.” That’s why he likes hanging out with the Lions.  At least he’s not bothered by football experts.
-- Thom Fladung, June 11, 2003
How did we engage and surprise readers today? With Steve Schrader’s Morning Line, which deserves a Hall of Fame placement in the “engage and surprise readers” category.
-- Dale Parry, July 9, 2003
As usual … numerous folks told me how much they enjoyed your year-ender package. Except, of course, the Lions!
-- Gene Myers, Dec. 26,  2001

Steve, after a fine job as a hockey reporter today, goes back to editing and his usual Five-Ring Circus duties. Be gentle with him. He’s still recovering from being snubbed by Sergei Fedorov in the mixed zone. Steve says Sergei just walked past all the reporters without saying a word; my theory is that he was ignoring Steve because of all the Page 2 items about Anna.
-- Dave Robinson, Feb. 21, 2002

I used to leave the comics to read last, kind of as dessert, a reward for plowing through all the other dry stuff in the paper. But this week, I’m ending my reading with Second Season. The column is a delight and many mornings makes me laugh out loud. Wonderful stuff, Steve. One of the many reasons I hate for the playoff season to end.
-- Nancy Laughlin, June 4, 2002
AND ONE CLASSIC REPONSE FROM STEVE …
FYI, I edited Eric’s mountain lion story, in which he quoted the fictional Dr. I.M. Lyon. He spelled the name two different ways.
-- Steve Schrader, April 1, 2002
